$comment: Port-level wiring between the Frontend's blocks, declared as data. No integrated top-level exists in the RTL drop, so the validation subsystem generates its own integration harness (chain_harness_gen.py) from this map. Every connection is checkable against the manifests: named ports must exist and widths must agree — a rename or resize in a regenerated drop becomes a loud structural failure, not a silently unconnected net.
$provenance: What the manifests cannot say. `connections` here are edges whose consumer manifest has no `source` field yet — each is a filed finding against the Frontend and should be deleted the moment the manifest declares it (integration_map_gen.py reports redundant entries). glue, expr_glue, ties, requires and stubs carry their own `why`.

glue.why: cmd_gen's feedback interface carries a bank number only for ACTIVATE (fb_act_bank); its PRE/RD/WR pulses are bankless, yet bank_tracker needs cmd_pre_bank/cmd_rd_bank/cmd_wr_bank to track per-bank state. The harness registers the scheduler's cmd_bank one cycle so it aligns with the REGISTERED fb pulses. This is testbench glue standing in for a missing design signal — see the filed finding; the Frontend should add fb_pre_bank/fb_rd_bank/fb_wr_bank.

cmd_gen's feedback carries no aux tag, but data_path needs the issued command's aux to tag read responses (rd_rsp_aux). Registered one cycle to align with the registered fb_rd_valid/fb_wr_valid pulses. Same missing-feedback-signal gap as the bank workaround — covered by the filed fb-bank finding; the design wants fb_aux.

expr_glue.why: data_path buffers a write word when wb_port's write request is ACCEPTED (valid && we && ready). No single design port carries that event; it is the same accept condition cmd_queue enqueues on.

Nothing in the drop consumes zqcs_req: no scheduler or cmd_gen port accepts a ZQCS request, so periodic ZQ calibration can never be granted by the design itself — an integration gap (finding filed). The harness acks immediately so the calibration FSM does not wedge; the cal_zqcs monitor still observes every request.

ties.$why_init_done: FALLBACK when init_fsm is not instantiated (command-path harnesses): refresh_ctrl waits for init_done before counting tREFI, and a tied-low init_done would silently disable every refresh. When init_fsm IS instantiated, the real init_fsm.init_done connection takes precedence.
ties.$why_enable: init_fsm starts as soon as reset releases; the harness has no power-management layer to gate it.

requires.$comment: Support-block closure: instantiating a block pulls these in, because tied-zero substitutes for them are behaviourally wrong (a zeroed bank_act_allowed blocks every ACTIVATE; zeroed cfg timings erase every constraint).

stubs.$why: Something must sit on the far side of the DDR pins or every read returns the tied-off bus. A behavioral DRAM: ACT opens rows, WR stores the burst word, RD replies after CL. Testbench component — nothing judges the design against it.

standalone_ties.$comment: Ties for the edges a `standalone` path cuts: a single block judged on its own streams, for a drop that does not yet contain its neighbours (phase-by-phase integration). Every cut edge MUST be listed with a why, or chain_harness_gen refuses the path -- the ordinary zero tie-off is not allowed to stand in for a missing block. A standalone path also runs on a complete drop, so its evidence is comparable across phases.

wb_port.req_ready.why: cmd_queue absent: the environment accepts every request at once. The wb_port predictor judges the req stream (one request per host access, with its address/data/mask/we) and the Wishbone handshake; what the queue would do with it is Phase 3's question.

wb_port.rsp_valid.why: data_path absent: no read data ever returns. Reads stay pending; the predictor's completes_on rule emits no wb_rsp for them and the standalone path drives writes only (path stimulus_kinds).

wb_port.rsp_rdata.why: unused while rsp_valid is tied low

wb_port.rsp_aux.why: unused while rsp_valid is tied low

config_regs.sts_init_done.why: init_fsm absent: CTRL_STATUS reports no boot progress. The register-walk path judges every register's RW/RO/W1C/reserved-bit semantics and the CTRL_STATUS read must show the tied value; the live status bits are judged by path_14/15/16 once their sources are in the drop.

$history.why: the drop's manifests now declare these sources (Frontend2 manifest fix, d77dc12); the map generator reported them redundant
